commit_reviews.summary: A clean greenfield TypeScript scaffold for the static site generator story with standard ts-jest config and well-scoped dependencies (gray-matter, marked), matching the session-1 commit message convention.

lock file churn is large relative to the single feature
commit_reviews.summary: Adds canonical file-watching (chokidar) and WebSocket (ws) runtime dependencies for the SSG dev-server live-reload integration, with correctly synchronized lock file and @types placed in devDependencies.

problems: ctx._renderIndex is an untyped duck-typed escape hatch
index rendering not integrated into plugin lifecycle
template/layout errors (e.g. "Layout not found") lose their specific messages
diff truncated so full plugin.ts/types.ts impact unverified
commit_reviews.summary: Refactors template rendering out of build.ts into a plugin lifecycle pipeline, but smuggles index rendering through an untyped `_renderIndex` field on the plugin context.
Adds a coherent Handlebars template/layout/partial system to the SSG with proper type extension, CLI flag, and tests, but ships leftover dead code.

problems: cache keyed on absolute tmp paths (non-portable
cache file written outside repo layout via parent dir
dead cache entries accumulate per serve run
commit_reviews.summary: The commit introduces a caching layer keyed on absolute /tmp paths and writes/commits a generated cache artifact into the repo, which defeats cache portability and violates build-artifact hygiene.

compounding_issues: Sessions 1-3 grew monolithically (build.ts ballooned to ~240 lines, dev server written inline in serve.ts); session 4 required a large extraction rewrite instead of incremental evolution
Session 4's plugin extraction created a circular dependency chain build.ts -> plugin.ts -> plugins/index.ts -> devserver.ts -> build.ts, tolerated only by lazy require() in loadPlugins
DevServerPlugin is a name-only no-op registered in the plugin list while the real server logic lives in createDevServer outside the hook lifecycle, leaving the plugin abstraction partially un-honored
node_modules/ and dist/ were committed every session (5164 files in session 1), inflating commits and compounding repository noise throughout the story
key_decisions: Session 4's plugin system with lifecycle hooks (onStart/beforeBuild/onFile/afterBuild/onEnd) plus context-based shared state (_renderPage/_renderIndex), unifying markdown, template, and dev-server concerns
Handlebars as the template engine with layouts + partials and frontmatter-selected templates (session 2)
Building the dev server first as a monolithic serve.ts (session 3), then deliberately absorbing it into the plugin architecture (session 4)
Session 5's incremental build via sha256 content+template hashing and a .ssg-cache.json manifest, wired into the plugin onFile skip path
Sticking with TypeScript/gray-matter/marked/jest and enforcing tsc + jest in every session, growing the test suite monotonically from 11 to 48 tests
story_review.trajectory_description: Quality improved steadily across the arc. Each session ended green (tsc passed, jest suites 100% passing) while the test suite grew monotonically 11 -> 23 -> 30 -> 30 -> 48 tests, and session 4's refactor slimmed build.ts from roughly 440 lines to ~180 by extracting plugins, genuinely improving structure rather than just renaming code. Session 5 added a clean, well-tested caching abstraction (CacheManager) and the largest single test file (485 lines). Sessions also grew more efficient (step counts fell 25 -> 19 and cost per session shrank), though the dev server's always-on incremental mode and the no-op DevServerPlugin hint at a slightly incomplete integration of the new abstractions.
story_review.summary: A highly coherent, improving five-session arc that evolves a TypeScript static site generator from a monolith into a plugin-based architecture with incremental caching, held back only by minor architectural warts and consistent git hygiene noise.
